text: You're quickly typing a message, like 'Happy birthday!' The small keyboard can be tricky. You just want your thoughts down fast, without mistakes.
Suddenly, your phone suggests 'birthday'. Then, after 'Happy birthday', it offers 'to you!' How did it know? It feels like it's reading your mind, predicting your next word.
Is your phone a secret psychic, or just guessing? The idea of a tiny fortune teller in your device is fun, but incorrect.
The real system is statistical. Your phone analyzed billions of sentences, finding patterns. It knows 'happy' often precedes 'birthday,' and 'birthday' by 'to you.'
It doesn't understand meaning, only probability. It predicts the most common next word. This engine also learns from *your* unique typing habits.
So, your phone isn't a mind-reader, but a clever pattern-finder. It's an invisible system, making your digital life faster, one predicted word at a time.
